out: One thing I often hear from people is how their inner child doesn’t trust them, usually despite the fact that the person has just said 3 nice things to him/her in meditation.

To this I respond with a few things. First of all, we have three ‘adults’ (that is aspects of the present day person) to do reparenting: the Nurturer, the Protector and the Leader/Guru. It’s important to keep in mind that these ‘adults’ are not separate people inside you, but merely the different functions of the present day person that are used for reparenting.

Secondly, the inner child also has something to offer. Besides being innocent and not having done anything to deserve the way they were treated, the inner child also has play, tenderness, irreverence, creativity, etc. to offer. And keep in mind that regardless of all that, the inner child is still worthy of love.
What to do if you cannot be your own parent yet

Thirdly, it often happens that people either can’t conjure up one of the above functions of the adult, or feel blank when they try, or only experience the ‘inherited internal critic’. Sometimes the problem is that the ‘adult’ doesn’t really feel like an adult, but instead feels like a child that is pretending to be an adult.

To solve this problem I use a technique that as far as I know, I developed (or at least combined in this way). I have no idea if it has been tried with people in therapy and if it works when all the parts are combined, but I find that it works for me.
Bring the Adult in by witnessing if that is necessary. If you can already differentiate the different ‘positions’ easily, skip this step and bring in the Adult that you need for this situation.

Borrow one of the Adult functions from someone else. Find a person in your life, a mentor, an older brother/sister, your own future self, a spiritual being, a value etc. that you think can be an Adult to you. Ask yourself what that person would say or do in the situation where you need that particular function (warmth, setting boundaries, knowing what’s best etc.) Be sure to only borrow what you need.
Now you become an apprentice of the Adult. Figure out yourself how you can say/do what you need in the situation. Make sure you at least do some of it yourself.
Now give the Adult functions back to the ‘borrowed’ person by telling them what they did and what 5% you can do now on your own.

It’s important not to let the ‘borrowed’ person take over your Adult functions, but to have them stand by you while you make the decision. For a more complete description of this, see my Inner Child Self Love Reparenting Guide .

Note: If you don’t have anyone in your life that you can remember that was a decent caretaker, then imagine someone who was, and make sure when you imagine what they would do, that you take into account your history. If you cannot even imagine being taken care of properly, start with ‘what the least cruel thing they could say/do?’ and when that starts working, move on to something better. Don’t keep doing variations of this exercise. Once you find something that works, try it out.

Also, you can use this technique when you feel that the ‘Adult’ doesn’t really feel like an adult. Ask yourself what a decent adult would do when the inner child says he/she doesn’t trust you. Don’t retaliate, don’t defend yourself by saying how good you are, don’t collapse and don’t leave. Just borrow one thing that a decent adult would do, even if you don’t feel old enough yet. You’ll get old later.
Let the Child speak without taking over Adult functions
While the above is happening, you may allow the ‘younger’ feeling state to come out and speak, but don’t give your Adult judgement functions to an outside ‘caretaker’ and don’t make yourself younger.

A good way to do this is to say something like: ‘You are allowed to speak, but know that my Adult is still here and will evaluate the situation and take care of you and will stop you if need be. I am not going into a younger state, neither am I going to listen to a guide, a recording or anyone else but my own Adult.’

This way you can get in touch with your wonder, playfulness, spontaneity, sensory perceptions, ability to express your needs and ability to quickly go from one emotion to the next, without also bringing in being obedient, helpless, scolding yourself and losing your Adult judgement.
Finally, even if the younger state doesn’t trust your love for him/her yet, that doesn’t mean that you can’t still love him/her.

Okay. I know that you don't believe me. And that's okay. I know that I still love you. And I know that you don't have to love me. But just tell me if there's something that you feel is not safe for you in what I'm doing, okay?

But that's not how we end a complaint. Be serious. When they hear our anger and don't retaliate, when we admit we really fucked up, when we repair with the position that attacked us internally, just like when we show up to make meals, set boundaries, go to appointments, and keep promises, all of this is part of the pattern of evidence to back up our words. It might feel like not retaliating when they're angry is a way of showing our love, but it doesn't replace having love; it doesn't make our love any less cold.

When they make a vow and then blame us for not believing them, notice if the one who's blaming and the one who's making the vow are a younger or older version of the same position, or if they're a blended position. Don't assume based on their chronological age.

Notice what it is they're trying to teach you. If you're in the position of the one being blamed, remember that you're in the position of a younger version of yourself. You didn't know what you know now. You made the best choice you could in that moment that you were willing to be aware of, with the consequences that resulted. Just because you did something harmful to someone (even if it's yourself) doesn't mean that punishing yourself helps. You still may need to take responsibility and make repairs, but punishing yourself isn't helpful.
The Two-Hand Practice
Place your hand over your chest (at your heart center) to connect with your ability to love physically. Place your other hand below your chest at your solar plexus to relate to the vulnerable child.
Send love from your heart to your child. See what you get back. It might take a few rounds for you to have a conversation.
Remember: The love is on top. The child is on the bottom. And you're in the middle.
The Nurturer
Your role as the nurturer is to offer your love and enjoy their company. It's as simple as that.
It's okay. I'm here. You don't have to do anything. You're not too much. You can be small. You can be angry. You can be sad. I'll be okay.
The Protector
Your job as the protector is to make the love feel real by protecting them.

I'll set that boundary. I won't engage in that unsafe conversation. I won't text that person. I'll make myself eat. I'll go to sleep. I'll keep that promise. I won't let you be responsible for adult stuff.

This is where a lot of people bullshit themselves when working with their inner child. As the adult, they may send destabilizing messages, fail to take care of themselves, not do what they need to do, and not keep promises. It starts to become real when you do the thing.

If you can't find the love, do the thing. It might be that you don't do the thing for the child, so figure out what's going on that's keeping you from doing the thing. It might not be that you're failing. It might just be that you were afraid, or tired, or didn't have the skills or didn't plan it out well, or whatever. Also, just because you didn't feel better right away doesn't mean that it didn't work. And just because you checked it off your list doesn't mean that it worked.
The Leader/Guide/Guru/Wise One/Sage/Inner Teacher/Director/Higher Adult
Your role in this triad is to give direction.

Sometimes that direction is hard. It's not always about being perfectly disciplined, but it's also okay for you to be the one to ask for help, to communicate what you want, to show your imperfections to safe people. It's okay to want to be close to people, but it's not okay to punish them when they need space. Figure out how to have it both ways.

You are here not just to feel good You are here to become whole You are here to be part of life You are here to serve truth, beauty and love You are here to serve God, source, nature, universe, dharma, Tao You are here to be of benefit to all beings
What will a healthy, mature adult do here? How can I get their help first?
Are protectors a useful way of putting it for you?
Most people assume that when I work with their inner child that I go straight to the child. That is rarely the case.

More often than not when I try and connect with their inner child… They go numb Or cynical Or angry Or hungry Or they feel the need to check their phone Or they feel a sexual urge Or they start planning their next day Or they go to sleep Or they dissociate Or they say “this is stupid” …

Another important voice is the inherited parent voice. This is the voice of the parent(s) the person has internalised as a child. It is different to my concept of the inner adult (Nurturer, Protector, Leader/Guru) which we work to create. Often this inherited parent voice is a critic or a warden. It tells the inner child not to cry, not to be needy, not to act in a way that would embarrass the parent, not to be independent, etc. This voice can often say “this isn’t real, this is fake, you’re just making this up” etc. when we try and bring in new, loving parent voices for the inner child.
What might this voice/feeling/urge be protecting me from? What might it be protecting my inner child from? How might I acknowledge this part and ask for it’s cooperation?

What might it be afraid would happen if it wasn’t here? If I wasn’t numb/cynical/angry/distracted? Would I be… Lying to myself Engaging in fantasy Engaging in a role Allowing myself to feel a pain that would destroy me Being spiritual instead of real Forgiving too soon Hearing a voice in my head that isn’t real Abandoning myself/my child at the end of the therapy session …
What can I do to gain this protector’s trust? Increase my trust by 1%?

What does this protector need from me? Usually it just needs me to do something simple: Keep a boundary Do a task Eat a meal Not send a text/message Keep a promise Go to sleep Make contact with my therapist Acknowledge a debt Write something down …
How might I protect myself in a more healthy, effective way?

The Protector isn’t just a voice in your head. It is also a way of moving through your body: Orient yourself Assess the situation Distinguish between real danger, uncertainty, and imagined danger Do one thing to protect yourself in proportion to the danger Assess if you are safe now Stand down from protection and let yourself rest …
The Protector is also a way of thinking: Acknowledge what you don’t know Ask other humans for help Refrain from interpreting things until you have more information Engage in “no trance” practice …
How might I reparent my inner child in this moment?

Reparenting therapy and self hypnosis are a perfect match. Sometimes the inner child will come forward as an age, an image, a body position, a voice, a memory, an emotion, or a sense of vulnerability. Often they won’t. That’s OK. Work with whatever you can identify: a protector, a sensation, a feeling, a preference, etc.
What to do once you see the child (TL;DR: Be with them for now, don’t try to heal them. Do this:
“ Hey, kiddo. It’s okay. I’m here. No need to talk. It’s okay that you’re like this. I’m not gonna try to heal you right now. You don’t need to impress me. What do you need? ”

Maybe they want to play, feel warm, be protected, grieve, be mad, eat, rest, push you away, be kept away from someone, stop fantasising, stop working too hard, or simply hear you promise that you will do something as an adult today for them.
Don’t rush to fix them. Take your time to:
1. Prepare yourself
2. Inspect the problem
3. Ask them what they need (warmth, contact, talking, space, nothing…)
4. Give them what they need (only one thing at a time)
5. Wait
6. Try to reconnect (don’t force the child to become a part of you, be a part of you, disappear, ‘forgive’ you, be happy…)
7. Rest
8. Evaluate the situation again later.

Remember, you don’t need to fix them completely and make them ‘good as new’, but ‘good as you’. If the term ‘parts’/’child parts’ is confusing to you, think of them as signals, feelings, younger versions of you, or whatever works.

Remember that even playing and resting require the ‘adult’ to be present - you’re not actually a child again, you don’t need to lose reality-testing in ‘re-parenting’. You’re not a child, pet, object or a doll that someone else owns, you’re you and you’re just trying to feel the emotions you missed out on. Play with a plushie, talk to it, draw, touch interesting things, do whatever seems interesting to the younger version of you.

When resting, remind yourself you don’t need to be completely helpless, but you can give yourself a break from making decisions for a set amount of time. You can also remind yourself that you can do the things you were supposed to do later, write them down so the ‘adult’ can see them later, while the ‘child’ rests. The ‘adult’ can also keep an eye out while the ‘child’ rests.

If you can’t talk to your ‘child’ or imagine a conversation, write it down, preferably using your non-dominant hand as the ‘child’ (or the protector you’re communicating with) and your dominant hand as the ‘adult’. It may feel weird and your handwriting will be bad, but it can work. E.g.
N-d h: I don’t trust you.
D h: That’s okay. I still love you. What did I do that made you feel that way? I won’t make you trust me, I’ll just hear you out and then promise to do something.
N-d h: What?
D h: Eat, clean my desk, not text that person…

old: Sometimes the inner-child question lands nowhere because a private self had very little room to develop. In controlling families, rigid religions, enmeshed communities, or high-pressure achievement systems, performance can begin so early that a person doesn’t know what they feel, want, believe, or prefer until somebody else tells them first. Then “love yourself” produces a reasonable question: love whom? Reparenting and identity-building can proceed together. For some people the child-self is already easy to feel. For others, creating enough safety for preference, curiosity, and experimentation is part of how that self becomes easier to hear.
This may apply when:
You do not know what you want unless someone else says what they want first.
Your opinions shift dramatically depending on who is in the room.
You agree in the moment and later realize you did not agree.
You feel responsible for other people’s emotions to the point of self-erasure.
Self-love feels performative.
The question “What does my inner child feel?” produces guesses, not felt answers.
You can rebel, but you cannot yet choose.

A useful developmental explanation is that when childhood is organized around avoiding pain and preserving attachment, attention goes into reading danger, meeting expectations, and keeping the bond. That can leave less room for the ordinary experiments that answer, “What do I like? What do I want to try? Who am I when nobody is grading me?” This is a practical model, not a claim about one specific brain system.

Sometimes a temporary, intentional period of distance from the people or group supplying the answers helps quieter preferences surface. Use that distance only long enough to tell your own signal from the social echo; prolonged isolation would undermine the purpose.

The difference between a human doer and a human being helps here. When worth isn’t felt internally, it gets earned through beauty, performance, intellect, status, spirituality, or becoming indispensable to everybody else. Those can all be real gifts. They become belonging bargains when failure in the arena feels like losing yourself.
Useful questions:

“What do I like when no one is watching?” “What do I believe before I check whether others approve?” “What do I want that is neither rebellion nor compliance?” “Where am I buying belonging with self-betrayal?” “Which arena am I using to earn the right to belong?” “What would I try if nobody needed to be impressed?” “Which relationships let me remain myself?” “What am I noticing in my body, and what meaning am I giving it?”

Give the inner child a small experiment with no résumé value: painting, dancing, gardening, a language, a sport, volunteering, music, or anything else you’re allowed to be bad at. The inherited parent may demand immediate talent. The adult can answer, “We’re finding out whether we enjoy this, not proving our worth.” Give it enough repetitions to get past the humiliation of being a beginner.

For a child, belonging can feel like survival, so families, religions, romances, political tribes, spiritual groups, institutions, and online communities can reach astonishingly far into identity. Adulting means noticing where you buy belonging with self-betrayal, choosing your own ground, and learning that you can disappoint someone without disappearing. The subconscious contains a crowd of borrowed voices, which is why this belongs in a self-hypnosis guide.
“Where do I become less true in order to remain included?”
“What would belonging look like if I did not have to disappear?”

“Is this guidance, or is this a belonging program?” “Is this love, or is this fear of exclusion?” “Is this conscience, or is this conditioning?” “Is this devotion, or is this compliance?” “Is this rebellion, or is this freedom?”
Then wait for the body. It isn’t infallible, but it deserves a seat at the hearing.
new: Working with your inner child can be harder when you did not have a private self to begin with. This happens a lot when people come from a background where their family, religion or community took over their life very early on, or they were pressured to achieve in a certain way at a young age. This means that you don’t know who you are, what you feel, what you want, what you believe, what you like, or what you don’t like until you hear what someone else says first. This makes it hard to follow the advice to “love yourself” when you don’t know who “yourself” is. So in these cases, reparenting needs to go hand in hand with finding yourself. For some, it’s easy to work with their child-self because they can feel their child-self really easily. For others, it requires creating safety and playing around more to feel their child-self.
You might be in this camp if:
You don’t know what you want until you hear what someone else wants
You find that your opinions change dramatically depending on who is around
You catch yourself agreeing with someone when you didn’t agree in the moment
You tend to take responsibility for other people’s emotions to the detriment of yourself
Trying to love yourself feels like a performance
Trying to find out how your inner child feels, results in guesses instead of feeling
You find that you can rebel, but you can’t choose

The reason for this is that a part of your brain didn’t have the opportunity to explore “what do I like?” and “what do I want to try out?” because as a child you were focused on finding ways not to hurt yourself or lose attachment.

Sometimes it is necessary to distance yourself for a certain period from the people or group that you are getting your answers from so that you can distinguish between what you want and what you are told to want. However, you don’t need to do this for long – just long enough to differentiate what is yours from what is social.

This means moving from a “human doer” to a “human being”. If you don’t feel like you are good enough just because you exist, you will try to create a sense of worth by being beautiful, by doing something well, by being smart, by gaining status, by being more spiritual than everyone else, or by being needed. In all of these cases, you are essentially making a bargain with yourself – that as long as you are good at something (or good at being good for other people), you will be good enough to belong. And if you fall short in that arena, you feel that you are not good enough.
To help you find yourself, ask yourself these questions:
What do I like when no one is watching?
What do I believe before I check what other people think?
What do I want that is not in rebellion to others, and is not in compliance with others?
Where am I buying my sense of belonging by betraying myself?
What “arena” am I using to try to buy my sense of belonging?
What can I try on for size that I don’t need to impress anyone with?
What relationships allow me to be myself?
What do I notice in my body and what meaning am I attaching to it?

Remember that your inner child needs to play! Try out some things that have no value towards your resume – painting, dancing, gardening, learning a language, a sport, volunteering, playing music, etc. Your parent may be telling you that you are supposed to be good at something as soon as you start doing it. Your job as your own parent is to remind yourself that you are not doing these things to prove your worth – you are doing them to see if you like them or not. And it will take some time before the humiliation of being a beginner goes away.

As a child, belonging was essential to your survival. As an adult, it can manifest in families, religions, romantic relationships, political tribes, spiritual groups, institutions, or even online. Part of “adulting” is finding out where you are trading your sense of self in exchange for belonging, and then consciously choosing where you want to belong – on your terms. A large part of your subconscious mind is made up of the voices of other people, so this is also a good opportunity to use some of the tools in this self-hypnosis guide to help you let go of them.
Where am I betraying myself in exchange for belonging?
What would it feel like to belong without having to betray myself?
Is this my own guidance or a belonging program I adopted?
Is this love, or is it a fear of being excluded?
Is this my conscience or is it conditioning?
Is this devotion, or is it compliance?
Is this rebellion, or is it freedom?
Then see what your body tells you.

old: Self-hypnosis also teaches influence literacy: noticing when somebody else is already shaping your attention. Screens, advertising, politics, religious fear, erotic imprinting, charismatic authority, belonging pressure, shame, urgency, and repetition all do it. Influence is everywhere—a lullaby, a prayer, a good teacher, a beautiful song, love. Ask what it does to your ability to see and choose.
new: One of the best side-effects of learning self-hypnosis is an increased awareness of all the ways you’re being manipulated in your day-to-day life. By a screen? By a specific ad? By a politician? By a religion? By erotic imprinting? By an authority figure? By the desire for belonging? By shame? By a sense of urgency? By repetition? It’s all around you. Sometimes it’s benign – like lullabies or prayers or being taught by a good teacher or listening to a beautiful song or being in love. But you may want to ask yourself what effect it’s having on your ability to see clearly and make choices.

old: Manipulation often arrives with urgency, specialness, fear of missing out, threatened exclusion, sexual charge, shame, confusion, rescue fantasy, destiny, obedience, secret knowledge, or far too much certainty arriving far too quickly. You may also feel that one honest question would break the spell.
new: Some common ways you may know you’re being manipulated include a sense of urgency, a sense of specialness, FOMO, being made to feel like you won’t be included if you don’t go along, sexual charge, shame, being confused, a fantasy of being rescued, a sense of destiny, a sense that you should obey, a sense of secret knowledge, or an excessive sense of certainty about something pretty quickly.

old: Pause there. Don’t obey immediately, and don’t perform automatic rebellion either. Wake up inside the influence.
new: If you’re being hypnotically influenced, stop. Don’t listen. Don’t rebel, either, just stop and realize that you’re being influenced.

old: Hypnotic language turns manipulative when it smuggles in your consent, makes one choice seem inevitable, or hides a disputed claim inside the sentence.
new: Some common ways hypnotic language becomes manipulative includes:

old: “When you finally admit…” “As you realize I’m right…” “The only reason you resist is…” “Part of you already knows…” “Your higher self wants…” “Everyone who is truly awake understands…” “If you doubt this, that proves your ego is afraid.”
new: “you’ll realize, eventually, that…” “you may eventually admit that…” “the reason you’re not feeling it yet is…” “even if part of you doesn’t feel that’s true…” “your higher self knows…” “everyone knows…” “the reason you don’t believe that’s true is your ego’s fear of…”

old: The grammar assumes the conclusion, turns resistance into proof, and makes obedience feel like awakening.
new: Other language patterns to watch out for include:

old: “What exactly is being claimed?” “What choice is being framed as inevitable?” “What is being presupposed?” “Who benefits if I accept this frame?” “What emotion is being amplified?” “What information is missing?” “Can I say no without being punished, shamed, mocked, abandoned, or spiritually downgraded?”
new: Is it telling you what you’re going to do or experience? Is there an implied lack of choice? Is it presupposing things that may not be true? Who benefits from you being in this frame of mind? Is it ramping up emotions that aren’t serving you? Is it not giving you information you should have? Can you easily say “no” without there being consequences (shame, getting mocked, not being let into the group, being labeled “unspiritual,” etc.)?

old: A useful guide leaves the adult self more present. Powerful states need stronger boundaries.
new: Even a good guide should be helping you to bring your adult self into the experience more. The more powerful the state, the more you should have boundaries.

old: Permissive words can still conceal coercion. I watch for the following:
new: Language that’s permissive but that still takes your choice away includes:

old: Indirect suggestion can slip past the skeptical guard because the conscious mind may never receive one clean proposition to accept or reject. The intended direction can still be quite specific even when the wording feels open, vague, conversational, or merely suggestive.
new: Utilizing indirect patterns, which often work better because they bypass the conscious mind, but can be specific about where they’re going even if vague in their language, may just seem conversational, or use suggestions.

old: Induction hidden inside explanation: attention is being narrowed while the speaker pretends only to inform. Even an “anti-hypnosis” lesson can use induction mechanics.
new: Using induction patterns while seeming to “explain” things (even some of my explanations of how to avoid hypnosis use some of the mechanics of induction).

old: Every answer means compliance: “yes,” “no,” noticing, not noticing, resistance, and silence are all redefined as proof that the suggestion is working.
new: Setting it up so that any response the listener gives is compliance (answering “yes” or “no,” noticing something, not noticing something, resisting, not responding).

old: “Whether you notice it or not” binds: uncertainty is converted into invisible success that cannot be checked.
new: Using bind patterns (“whether or not you notice…”).

old: Identity and ownership language: safety or goodness becomes tied to obedience, a role, the guide’s approval, or belonging to someone else.
new: Telling you who you are or using language that makes you feel like you “belong” to the guide or that being “good” or “safe” comes from obeying the guide or a role.

old: Unannounced fractionation: moving in and out of absorption without telling you that repeated re-entry is part of the method.
new: Fractionating you without telling you they’re doing it.

old: Hidden post-session cues: words, gestures, blinks, sounds, or repeated listening are meant to produce later behavior that was not plainly disclosed.
new: Using post-session cues (gestures, blinks, sounds, even having you listen to something more than once) that they haven’t told you about that will make you do something later.

old: Amnesia or truth inflation: dreamlike material, missing memory, imagery, or body sensations are treated as proof of what happened.
new: Making you forget things, telling you something is true, utilizing “dream logic,” utilizing imagery or body sensations to make you believe something is true.

old: An exit that does not exit: the recording ends while preserving a role, reduced judgment, impaired movement, blankness, or an indefinite altered state.
new: Not actually letting you “out” at the end of the recording, leaving you in a role, or leaving you in a state where your ability to use good judgment or move your body is impaired or leaving you blank or in an altered state for an indefinite amount of time.

old: A real choice includes at least one branch that doesn’t continue the induction: make it lighter, change the method, remain fully alert, pause, or stop. No remains no. Silence and uncertainty don’t become consent because the narrator has a soothing voice.
new: Make sure you have a real choice to not proceed with the induction at any time, make it more gentle, use a different way, not be in an altered state at all, or stop or pause the induction and know that “no” really means “no.” Even not responding or not being sure should not be taken for “yes” just because someone’s voice sounds nice.

new: For a longer de-hypnosis checklist, see Appendix C.

out: Induction: gathering attention without disappearing

Hypnotic inductions are techniques to gather your attention so you can get to the good stuff quicker. They are NOT about giving in, playing asleep, being gullible or letting someone control you. The "actual induction" part is most useful when you are sober, distracted, analytical or closed down. If you are already trancey (meditation, loveyhuasca, lucid dreams, falling apart from grief, music, prayer, tired or other intense experiences) skip straight to the "orientation and containment" part.
Generally, you want to go just deep enough to be very focused, warm, receptive, embodied and able to stop when you want to. You can go deeper if you want but it is not needed.
What are you doing when you do an induction?

You are preparing for a session. This can include getting focused, getting deeper and using utilization (shaping what you say according to what you are noticing happening). There are many ways to "get in" - counting is often used, but conversational, stories, movement, sounds, curiosity etc. can work. Using other ways is fine, just mention you are doing it - don't try to be "clever" and do it behind someone's back!

You can do a simple target and test for it to see if you need to go deeper to get the response you are after. If you are getting it, you may not need to. Learning to listen in a receptive way is one of the benefits of doing an induction. It is not a ritual or ceremony that has to be "completed" before you can respond.
Please, no more than 6 metaphors in one trance!

Have a purpose - do one thing. Have a way to start - an anchor or an image that orients you. Have a way to get back. Have a tone - it can be warm and caring or more solid and boundary oriented or it can provide direction or it can be neutral and witnessing. Choose your world / metaphor / image / feeling (floating, stairs, gardens, going to an inner place, seeing colors, talking to a child part etc. It is OK to change them but do it consciously.

You do not have to use imagery. You can receive signals in many ways: sensations, rhythms, movements, words, spatial, knowing, lack of response etc. Keep your language in your chosen world. If you count, relate the counting to your world and remember to do the opposite to get back. You can borrow qualities (warmth, steadiness etc.) but not identities.
Use a central verb, a sensory quality, a short refrain and a transition to put you in your chosen world. Read the induction script out loud. Long elegant sentences turn to soup during an induction.
What to do before an induction

Read the induction and "come all the way back" parts while fully awake. Choose what you want to do - a question to ask, a quality to bring in etc. Also choose what you are NOT going to bring in this session. Have a purpose that lights you up - love, play, confidence, creativity, communion etc. Consider how long you want to spend and allow a few minutes to come back and reflect afterwards.

Make sure you are in a safe physical place - don't do this if you are driving, in the water, near machinery or need to take care of people. Don't do this if you are intoxicated or acutely confused - if you need support, get it. (The section on "Already open?" at the end is designed to orient, not intensify an unstable state).

Choose a supportive tone for yourself - warm and caring, solid, directional or neutral. Prepare for what is going to happen - close your eyes, go in and out a few times and come all the way back. If you are going to use a recording, read the script if possible. Know that you can stop at any time by saying "Stop", you can reduce the demands on you by saying "Less", you can have the words stop by saying "Quiet" or you can just open your eyes and be done. You don't even have to get the OK from any part inside.

If you have never tried this, practice going in and coming back before you bring in a difficult subject. Once you know how to change states, you don't need to be a supervisor to your own life. You can learn to allow things to happen with less effort. The answer "No" will stay "No" and someone won't pop into your head and start talking if no one was there before.

To learn how to shape what you are saying to fit what is happening (utilization), see Appendix B and how to use it after the induction, see "Let the next response guide you". Notice what does happen - sometimes nothing will change and that may mean that the change already happened. If you are not clear about the safety and exit instructions, read them again.
An induction to use when sober (3 - 5 minutes)

Read this slowly into a recorder or read it out loud. You can even do it in your head if you are skilled at silent words. Choose an anchor (sound, body contact, two hands practice etc.) and an opening phrase and stick with them when you come to the anchoring phrases in the script. Don't read the directions aloud. Pause between paragraphs.
Where would your eyes like to rest right now? Perhaps just staring off into the room a bit?

Where are you making contact with the surface beneath you, right now? Can you just sit with that contact a bit, while perhaps turning your attention to some sounds you hear, or the feeling of your breath?
Give this a bit of time.

Even if there are thoughts that come to mind about your day, about doing this right, etc., can you find a way to move your attention back to that anchoring point, while just noticing the thought a bit?
Just letting one particular aspect of that sound, or contact with the surface, or the contact of listening itself, hold your attention for a bit?
Give yourself the time you would give a loved one who was beginning to speak to you but hadn’t quite finished yet. Just being with them while they spoke.
Perhaps by saying to yourself, in your head, some phrase you’ve chosen in advance, and noticing how that phrase is received by you.
You can let your eyes close, or soften, or be open, as you feel you like, while continuing to listen, perhaps letting the sound you’ve chosen become more like background noise.
Perhaps counting backwards from 5 to 1, slowly.

Noticing again your chosen anchoring point, as you count 5, 4, allowing the noticing to gather a bit, 3, allowing a bit of space after you speak the word, 2, listening into the space, 1, and just being there for a moment.
Bring to mind, perhaps, something you would like to bring into contact with, or an issue you’ve chosen to bring to this.
What do you notice in response to that?
Give yourself some time to notice what form that response takes, if any. Sensations, words, images, feelings, moves, etc.
Allow some time to just notice, with or without words.

You are already in an open state (caused by loveyhuasca, a previous meditation, an impending lucid dream, an intense moment of grief, beautiful music, prayer, erotic energy, exhaustion, experiencing something of great beauty, etc), and want to contain it enough to then deepen it.
Recognize that you are already in an open state and don’t need to enhance the openness of the state, just aim and stabilize it in a kind way.

Begin by getting yourself oriented. Look around the room, say where you are, what date it is, etc. Feel your body parts. Apply some pressure with your thumbs on your index fingers, and focus on the physical sensation of the friction between the two.

Say to yourself, “I only wish to bring forth what I am able to integrate at this time. If there is more, it can wait until I am able to deal with it. I will keep my body safe. I will keep my adult self present while also being with any parts of my inner child that wish to come forward.
Once oriented, choose one of the following phrases:
“Please show me what you wish to show me, be it truth, symbols, feelings, questions, actions, etc., that is useful for me to know, in a dosed form that I am able to integrate.”
You find yourself losing track of time in your mind when trying to meditate
Sit up, open your eyes, feel your feet, etc.
“ I am not going to leave my body and head somewhere else in my mind. Instead, I am going to come into contact with what is here , now .”
Look at an object, feel your spine, etc.
“Is what I am experiencing now a daydream that is serving as a vehicle for my higher self to guide me, a way of working through some issue emotionally, or a way of avoiding something in the present?

Whatever it is, please direct my daydream in a way that will benefit me. If it is a vehicle for my higher self, please direct my daydream toward a conclusion that gives me some idea of what actions to take. If it is a way for me to work through some issue, please direct the daydream to some conclusion that helps me do that. If it is a way for me to avoid something in the present, please bring me gently back to the present and let me know in whatever way is best for me what I am avoiding.”
Hypnosis for people who can’t sit still and quiet in their bodies or heads without drifting into sleep, diffusion, or other forms of escape.

Open your eyes. Say to yourself, “As I press my thumb and forefinger together, I will become more and more clear in my body and head. As I release the pressure, I will maintain that clarity.” Press your thumb and forefinger together and release a few times. Then say to yourself, “I will now stop the deliberate movement of my fingers, and notice what happens in the first second after I stop the motion, and any aftereffects I might feel from it.” Stop the movement of your fingers, and see if there is some effect you can feel, or not. Continue working at this level.
Two hand induction :
put one hand on your heart, one on your solar plexius
Think of the hand on your heart as your nurturer, and the one on your solar plexius as your vulnerable child.
Then breathe and say to yourself
Love above, child below, adult present.
Love above, child below, adult present. Love above, child below, adult present. Etcetera.
Induction for sleep

It's a bit different for sleep, since you're not going to have your adult coming back, writing things down and taking action. It's kind of cheating, and at bedtime you don't want your analyzing self to be on duty. If you want something to happen or to know, it can wait till later.
Check out Nimja's sleep playlist for sleep hypnosis:
Fractionation (optional)
Once you've taught it, you can use fractionation. It's not good to sneak it in, since not everything needs to be deeper. Here's how to teach it:

Open your eyes and come back up. You can stop the exercise now, if you want to. You can also, if you want to continue, close or soften your eyes, and notice how your attention is gathering again. You can stop again at this point.
You can continue to let your focus gather, if it's useful for you to do so. If it's not useful, you'll be as awake as you need to be.

Picture yourself in your inner meeting place. It might be a room in your heart, a garden, a temple, sitting by a fire with your Protector nearby, at the side of a clear lake, sitting in a chair as your adult self. Just pick one, you don't need more.
Ask yourself who or what might need to talk first.
Trance check (optional)
See if your letting go of the responsibility for making it happen

That if it's useful for you to do so, your wise subconscious can make one of your fingers twitch, pulse, lift up, warm up, tingle or do something subtle to let you know that you are ready to begin meeting with yourself inside.
That you won't force it or fake it, you'll just wait with love and see what happens.

It might be that your finger does something, your hand warms up, you notice your breathing or it might be that nothing happens. None of these proves anything, except perhaps that something inside is listening to you.
Shortcut to get back into hypnosis

This one you should only play with once you know an induction well, and how to come back up from it completely. My dad would often snap his middle finger and thumb together, kind of like a mudra or the OK signal, to help him relax, even while driving.

Pick a word or phrase, and a gesture if you want to. Pick something that is not likely to come up often in normal conversation. When you are in a nice state of hypnosis, not at a peak of emotional intensity, not in a child state or viewing a traumatic scene, but just generally in a state of being more receptive to what you are saying to yourself, say to yourself something like:

When I deliberately use this signal to myself at a time when I have set aside time to do this work, and at a place where it is appropriate to do this work, I will come back into this state of being more receptive to my inner guidance. I can always change that or come out of it, just like I can now.

Then come all the way back up. At another appropriate time, when you are deliberately starting the work, practice using your shortcut. It may take a while to establish, there is no need for it to be instant, there is no need for a specific number of repetitions to establish it, and there is no need for any particular sensation to be associated with it. If you find that the shortcut works well, you can make the longer induction shorter. If you find that it isn't working for you, you can always use the longer induction.

See if it is useful for you, and see if it is selective enough to not be activated when you don't want it to. Make sure that you can change it and that you can come back up from it. It should not be used to make you do something that you might not want to do when you hear the word, phrase or gesture. It should not make you go into a hypnotic state when you see a notification on your phone, hear someone else say the word or phrase, or overhear it in conversation. How fast you get into hypnosis does not determine how deep you can go with the work.

Do not practice or use this to get yourself back into hypnosis while you are driving or doing something that requires your active attention, even if you open your eyes and even if you phrase it conditionally.

If you want to eliminate the shortcut, stop rehearsing it, stop including it in recordings or active instructions in apps and just go back to the original induction. You don't need to say anything to eliminate it, although saying something to yourself when you are fully awake won't hurt. If you find that you are still responding to it when you don't want to, or if you find yourself disoriented, you can always seek help from someone qualified. If you do want to keep it around, you should only use it to start a new session at a later date, and not to alter your state while you are already working.

old: Reverse whatever you used to enter. If you floated, regain chosen weight. If you became small, return to ordinary scale. If you met a younger state or several parts, confirm present wholeness, body ownership, and adult judgment. If you traveled, come back by the same route. Keep only the qualities you deliberately chose.
new: Come out of the session by reversing the entry method; if you floated, come back down by the same method; land with your chosen weight. If you shrunk, come back to your normal size. If you meet your younger self or parts, make sure that you acknowledge that you are now whole, this is your body, and you are using your adult judgement. If you traveled, then come back the same way you left. Make sure that you are only bringing back what you had intended to bring back.

All instructions to deepen or remain in this session are finished. I keep only the ordinary-life intention or future-practice cue I consciously chose; neither keeps today’s altered state running. I am myself, in my body, with adult judgment fully available.”
new: You may wish to say, “I am bringing back only that which I choose to bring back at this time. All that is not needed at this time will remain safely stored away until such time as I am ready. I am now coming back to this place and to my body and to normal day to day living. All instructions given to me in this session are now over except for the conscious intention (or cue) to implement in the future.”

old: One — feel the body’s contact and chosen weight. Two — let the breath return to its ordinary rhythm. Three — hear the room and name where you are. Four — move fingers, toes, shoulders, and eyes. Five — eyes open, present, ordinary, clear. The session has ended.

Coming back to awareness of your surroundings and of your location. 4. Moving your fingers and your toes and your shoulders and your eyes. 5. Opening your eyes, feeling present, normal and clear. Your session is now over.

Check that you are actually oriented and alert; repeating the count is not proof of a complete return. Note only what actually appeared, and any action it calls for. Then do something normal.
new: It is a good idea to say to yourself what day it is or what the date is, look to your left and to your right, look at something near and something far away, move about a bit before you stand up, stand up and make sure that you are oriented and alert. Take note of anything that came up during your session and what you may or may not need to do as a result, and then just go about doing something normal.

old: If a recording stops unexpectedly: say, “The recording stopped and the session is over.” Open your eyes, name the location and day, press your feet or hands into a surface, move, look around, and use the five-step count. Don’t wait for the missing narrator to release you.

However, if you are waking when the recording ends, then it should not leave you in any state that is not conducive to normal functioning, such as leaving you in a role, with lowered judgement, impaired movement capabilities, blank or with an undefined reset word, etc.

old: Sit rather than lie down when you tend to daydream, dissociate, or fall asleep. Let the spine rise without becoming military, soften the jaw, and keep some awareness of the room. Save lying down for sleep, deep rest, or dream incubation.
“I am not leaving life. I am listening more deeply to life.”
Begin by invoking the larger field:

“Higher Self, universal heart-mind, wise subconscious, body intelligence, inner child, inner adults, protective parts, and all that serves truth and love: please help me understand what I need to know, only in the form and timing that is useful, kind, stabilizing, and real.”
You’re asking the conscious mind to listen without forcing an answer.

Thoughts do not have to stop before deeper listening begins. Let thoughts, sensations, images, doubts, and emotions pass through awareness without fighting or following them; keep the intention lightly in the background and notice what becomes salient on its own.
“Please tell me what I need to know, or ask what you need to know. I will wait silently for five minutes.”
The response may be a phrase, sensation, memory, color, child, protector, pain, warmth, silence, task, gratitude, an urge to stop, or the realization that today’s practice is over.
Listen to all of it. Believe none of it automatically.
new: Make sure you are not lying down when you do this exercise, unless you are ready to go to sleep or receive deep rest or are trying to incubate dreams. Sit in a place where you will not find yourself daydreaming, dissociating or going to sleep. Keep your spine straight, but not rigid, like a soldier. Relax your jaw and maintain some connection with the room you are in.
You can say to yourself, “I’m not going to leave life, I’m just going to listen more deeply to life.”

Invoking: “With the help of my Higher Self, my universal heart-mind connection, my wise subconscious mind, the intelligence in my body, my inner child, my inner adults, my protective parts and everyone and everything else that can help me to know what I need to know, only what I need to know in a useful, kind, stabilizing, real way…
Ask your conscious mind to listen.

This doesn’t mean you have to silence your thoughts to listen. Notice your thoughts, sensations, images, doubts, emotions, etc., without fighting them, without going with them, but simply noticing them while you hold the intention of this exercise in the background of your mind. Notice what becomes salient to you.
You can say, “Tell me what I need to know or tell me what I need to know to ask, and I will sit in silence for five minutes and listen.”

You might hear a phrase, feel a sensation, notice a memory, see a color, be contacted by a child or protector, feel pain, warmth, silence or know that your need to do something or be grateful for something or that this is enough listening for today.
Listen to it all and believe none of it.

out: Let the next response guide you

This post is to be read after the induction and inner meet and is mostly about how to respond when you are actually doing the work. It would be a good idea to read through it before you start and then not have it on screen when you do the actual work.

Responding The most basic way of responding is to notice something accurately and then either offer a new invitation or something that brings in more and then acknowledge what happens and wait. When something comes up that you can notice like a sensation, image, gesture, feeling or words you can acknowledge that, for example:
Finding your own words
It feels like my chest is tightening when I imagine asking for help
Can I get some time before I decide what that means and notice what comes up.

And then just listen. It's perfectly OK to not be very good at constructing beautiful sentences to invite things. In fact it's probably better that you don't. Sometimes it is useful to stop talking when something is developing to let it get on with it without interruption, other times you need the words to understand what is happening.
If you want to be more forceful with yourself then be more forceful, for example:
Don't try to tell me what it means, just notice what you feel when you say that.

Be direct. You don't need to make everything you feel nice, you just need to not feel it the same way and be able to change direction if you want to. Being sad or feeling tension doesn't mean you have to change it.

Separating things out can be hard and they can be jumbled together. It's not essential that you separate them out but sometimes it's useful to do so and ask yourself some questions to check if your interpretations are correct, for example:

When I say "My stomach tightened" that's just a description of what happened inside you. When you say "That person is evil" you are making a conclusion. You may not even be saying it in words but it still counts. So then you can go back and look at what that person did, work out what cues you were responding to and whether there could be other reasons for what they did. You don't need to have said the sentence at the time, saying it now will help you examine it. The fact that something happened inside you and was non verbal doesn't mean that it is either more or less true than if it was verbal. It's just a feeling and feelings are fine to analyse.
Let the response change the invitation

When you notice something like "My shoulders tightened" or "It feels like that sentence is wrong" then you can work out if what you are saying is the right thing to say or not. If what you are saying doesn't fit then work out what does, just like in normal conversation. If the answer is an explicit NO then don't ask for anymore reasons, just change what you are doing.
Why does my shoulders tighten, can I leave it tightening and see if my invitation fits or if there is something else I want to do.

Quite often the sentence was wrong. Other times it's just that the idea that you are looking at is unfamiliar and you need to let that feeling develop. Remember that just because you are skeptical about something doesn't mean that you have an inner child or that it is protecting you, you might just be silent.
Look at the situation

If you are looking at something that involves other people then you can also look at what the other person is doing. It's OK to decide that someone else is not able to take responsibility or isn't emotionally mature enough to have a normal conversation with you. You don't have to be absolutely sure that they are, just that you think that they are, you don't have to repeatedly expose yourself to dangers.

You can also look at what you are doing in the situation. It's OK to feel guilty but remember that feeling guilty doesn't mean that you are doing something wrong or that someone else is trying to manipulate you. Look at what you are doing, are you doing something to someone else that you should address or are you letting someone else make you feel bad so that you give in to them. When you go into an interaction with someone else decide why you are doing it. Do you want to improve mutual understanding, are you trying to convey information or are you trying to say no and leave. You don't have to make someone understand something before you do something.
Change the amount of contact

If you find that you need to reduce contact then try and expand your attention to other things in the room or in your body to bring in some support. Pendulation and titration can be useful to learn about, they basically mean that you alternate between difficult things and things that are more manageable.
of those, you can let be present, here are some tips to help

If at any point you feel you are losing your sense of ‘now’, starting to feel unreal, and you cannot change it or stop it then stop doing the exploring and do the whole Come all the way back thing. If you still don’t feel in touch with reality you need real human help.

If you feel like moving, try a small, physically safe movement in the direction your body wants to move or just imagine making that movement. You do not have to move if you don’t want to or if you feel you need to shake or ‘let something out’. Don’t move if you feel it will cause pain or other bad symptoms.
Give what you are asked for

If you feel younger, try not to make yourself younger still or find out what ‘really’ happened. Just be with your younger self. If you feel like you have a protector, listen to what it has to say, but don’t force it to let you go on. Don’t force any ‘part’ of you to leave.
If there’s anything you need to say, say it, such as: ‘I’m here with you. Do you want me with you or do you want some space?’

If you are told not to get any nearer then don’t get any nearer and explore what it’s like to have said that. If you feel you have different parts of you, such as a Nurturer, Protector and Leader, then you can ask one to speak in the voice of another if that’s appropriate, otherwise just use their function. If you don’t have one of these then borrow one and use it for that function only. You don’t need to use the Witness unless you have to in order to start. If you can start without using the Witness don’t bother to start over.

If it feels like it might help, try putting your hands on yourself, or imagining someone else there, or saying something you think might help, or moving into a different position, or moving further away, or anything else you think might help just to see what effect it has.

Giving yourself love may bring up sadness about not having had enough, it doesn’t mean the love wasn’t there. Explore as long as you want to but don’t force yourself. If it feels like it’s not helping, try something different. If not being able to accept love is a problem for you and the way you’re doing this feels like it’s not helping then try something else.

If you prefer to think in metaphors you can explore things that way but don’t try to find out what it ‘means’. Just imagine what you think might help and see what happens. Don’t interpret what happens, it’s just a useful metaphor. It is not proof of what ‘really’ happened. Just try doing what you think might help if it hasn’t already been tried and see what happens.

If you want to develop more of a good feeling, such as love or playfulness, you can spend the whole session on that if you want to. You can use the time to rehearse something you want to do in ‘real life’.
Finish the session without forcing anything

When you feel like you’ve had enough, stop. You don’t have to find out anything else. You can ask if there’s anything you need to do to ‘put this away for now’. If you’ve talked to ‘parts’ of yourself, thank them for helping you. You don’t have to do anything, if there’s something you want to do in ‘real life’ such as eat something nice, or say no to someone, or rest, or repair something that’s broken, or keep a promise you’ve made to yourself, then that’s fine. If there isn’t anything you need to do that’s fine too.

Remember that you can use your ‘thinking brain’ throughout this. If there’s anything you want to find out the facts about, wait until you’ve come all the way back again. Don’t believe everything you ‘find out’ in this exercise.

When you’ve finished use the Come all the way back thing even if you stopped earlier than you intended. It may help to write down a few notes about what happened so you can remember it. You don’t need to make a detailed note of everything, just a few words to remind you of what happened. If there was a useful phrase that came up, or a bodily sensation, or a need from a ‘child’ part, or something a protector said, or a boundary you need to put in place, or something you need to repair, or something you need to not force yourself to do, write that down so you can remember it.

old: Use the same practice rather than learning a second script: gather attention, listen, respond, wait, return. Fifteen minutes is a convenient appointment with yourself, not a therapeutic dose or a timetable your feelings must follow. Use a few minutes to enter, leave several minutes to return, and let the middle unfold at its own pace. Five minutes of silent listening is available when useful; you can interrupt it to change direction.
new: You may choose to do all of this practice, or learn the second script. Either way, you'll be using a similar process and can use these recordings as a base for your own practice. These exercises only need to be done for fifteen minutes or so. This is not a therapeutic time, but merely enough time to induce yourself (a few minutes), do what you are going to do (in this case 5 minutes of sitting in silence and listening), and then bring yourself back out again (a few minutes). You can break out of the process at any time, if you feel you need to do something else.

old: Another simple entry is to notice three things you see, three you hear, and three bodily sensations; then two of each, then one. Count from five to one and begin listening. Use the entry that suits you, rather than stacking inductions.
new: B) Notice three things you can see, then three things you can hear and three sensations you can feel in your body. Now do two of each, then one of each. Count from 5 to 1 and start listening.

old: After familiar runs, shorten a recording to the cues you still need, then try practicing without playback. Keep recordings when you enjoy them; independence means being able to guide yourself, not having to refuse help. The optional re-entry cue can shorten an already familiar induction.
new: After practicing a few times with these scripts, feel free to edit them down and remove any parts that you feel are no longer necessary to help you induce yourself. The idea is that eventually, you will not even need to play them back. But there is no harm in using them if you enjoy it. (Note: in script A, the part about coming back out again is optional; if you are familiar with the induction process, it will probably be enough to simply count).

old: Afterward, ask what needed warmth, what needed protection, and what direction serves truth, love, and life. Was there something to explore, or capacity to build? What can you carry yourself now? When action is needed, make it concrete: “If [cue] happens, then I will [small action].” Check how you sleep, relate, and function later, not only how impressive the session felt.
new: When you come out of the process, consider whether there is anything you would like to nurture with more warmth, or protect, or direct in a way that moves it in the direction of truth and love and life. Perhaps there is something you would like to explore or build up. You may want to take this process with you as you move about your day. If there is something you need to do, then make a plan with yourself to do that thing. Be concrete and say something like, "If _________ , then I will do________ ." Then see how things are later on: how you are sleeping, relating and functioning.

old: Once or twice a week, give the same practice more time when that is useful. More time needn’t mean greater intensity. Start from Higher Self or neutral witnessing, follow what appears, borrow an adult function when needed, and ask whether anything important is being bypassed. Leave room for the full exit and any ordinary action needed afterward.
new: Practise this once or twice a week and spend a bit more time with it if that would be useful but don’t make the practice any stronger. Whenever it is useful just access Higher Self, or if that is not possible go to a neutral witnessing place and let it unfold, using any adult function that is necessary to recognise any bypassing that may be going on and always allowing for a full exit and any necessary normal action.

old: Do the ordinary action immediately when possible. That teaches the subconscious that the adult heard and acted, instead of staging another beautiful internal meeting and then leaving the dishes exactly where they were.
new: Wherever possible take any normal action immediately afterwards to impress on the subconscious that something has changed, otherwise it may think that because the dishes have not been done, despite all the internal meetings to do the dishes, that there is no point in doing them.

old: Altered-state rule: do not ask for hidden truth while medically unsafe, panicking, sleep-deprived, nauseated, destabilized, manic, psychosis-like, or chemically overwhelmed. First stabilize. Truth that requires destabilization is not ready to be known directly. Ask for capacity, not content.

Sometimes it feels as though the subconscious knows something the conscious mind can’t yet tolerate. The subject may be sexuality, grief, trauma, family truth, betrayal, shame, vocation, relationship reality, illness fears, spiritual calling, addiction, identity, or moral conflict.
Interrogation is the dangerous response:
“Tell me now.” “Reveal everything.” “Stop hiding.” “I demand the truth.”

That pressure can produce flooding, panic, false certainty, confabulation, dissociation, or a generally worse Tuesday. Flooding can make the adult capacities needed for pausing, comparing options, reality-testing, planning, and choosing much harder to reach. In that state, regulation and support come before deeper dialogue. Silence may be protection when the adult lacks enough regulation, support, humility, or practical capacity to receive the material.
Ask for the next tolerable piece:
“Do I need to know the content now, or do I need to build capacity first?”
“What would make the conscious mind 5% more able to receive this?”
“Can you show me the truth as a symbol, not a full revelation?”
“Can you give me the next protective action without revealing the whole story?”
“Who, if anyone, should help me hold this?”
A safer script:

“Wise subconscious, if there is something I cannot yet handle, please do not break it open violently. Help me become someone who can know it safely. Give me preparation before revelation. Give me grounding before memory. Give me support before intensity. Give me one next action.”

Hypnotic imagery can be meaningful without being literal. The mind symbolizes, compresses, distorts, dramatizes, and borrows from culture and fear. Around trauma and memory especially, treat an image as an image and involve outside support when needed.
new: NOTE: If it is medically unsafe for you to do this, or you are panicking, sleep deprived, nauseated, deeply destabilized, manic, in a psychosis-like state, or overwhelmed by chemicals, please stabilize first before seeking out what your subconscious needs you to know. It is not ready for you to know it if it requires you to destabilize to know it!

There are times when your subconscious seems to know something that it is difficult for your conscious mind to know. It may be about your sexuality, a grief, trauma, your family, betrayal, shame, vocation, a relationship, fears about illness, spirituality, an addiction, your identity, or a moral issue.
What you don’t want to do is bully your subconscious with statements like,
“Why don’t you just tell me?” “What are you hiding?” “Tell me right now!” or “I demand that you reveal the truth!”

This can lead to flooding, panic, false certainty, confabulation, dissociation, and just generally making your day suck more. When you’re flooded, it can be hard to access your adult capacities to pause, choose, reality test, plan and make choices for yourself. Until your adult has enough of these capacities, especially regulation and support, it is not good for your subconscious to communicate with you. Silence is safer. But when your adult does have enough regulation, support, humility, and other capacities, you can talk with your subconscious.

“What do you need for my conscious mind to be able to know what you’re saying 5% better?” “Can you tell me through a symbol?” “Can you tell me what you need me to do to be safe without telling me what it is?” “Do you need me to get support to be able to know what it is? Who?”

You may even want to say, “Dear wise subconscious mind, if there is something you know that my conscious mind can’t handle, please don’t just break it open in a way that isn’t good for me. Please prepare me to hear it in a way that is safe. Ground me. Get me support. Tell me what to do.”
REMEMBER: Hypnotic imagery is not always literal, especially around trauma and memory.

out: Troubleshooting
Nothing happens
If you're having problems, start by starting small .
What to do if something feels "fake"

First notice if it is the words, the picture, or what you are asked to do that feels fake. Note that if you don't hear a voice or see a picture, it does not mean that there is resistance, or that you cannot do adult things in the inside. But if it is something asked of you that you don't want to do, stop and correct it. If you sense that there is a part that doesn't want you to do it, you may want to find out what it is trying to protect you from. You might say something like, "I notice that you don't want me to do this. What are you trying to protect me from? Are you afraid that I'm going to fake it? Are you afraid that I am going to play pretend and that this will be like what I went through before?" etc.

It may be your parents' voice in your head trying to enforce the rules you used to need to belong to them. Don't argue with it; find out what rules it is enforcing, and then try to come up with evidence that will convince it that the new voice is more believable.

If you sense that you just don't have what you need yet to do a step, stop pushing yourself to have a voice that "sounds good." If you can at least observe yourself, you can ask for help to borrow what you need from someone else (real or imagined). Try the action or words and see how they are received.
What to do if the subconscious doesn't answer

It may be that there is no answer, or that the questions you are asking are not the right ones. Try different ones. If you prefer to stop, do that. If there is a part that is concerned about trusting your subconscious, find out what it needs. You might ask, for example, "What do you need to know before you will trust me?" You may find that the answer is extremely un-mystical, e.g., "You have to set a boundary." Or, "You have to promise to do ____." Or, "You can't keep leaving us." Or, "You have to stop doing intellectual substitutions for actually doing something."
What to do if your inner child won't show up

If you can tell that there is a guard, talk to it. If not, work with whatever you can sense. Even if it is just a feeling or a preference, you can say, "OK, you don't want to come out, that's fine. But can you at least tell me what you want?"
If you can't sense a child-state, then treat the session as an identity building session or do some reparenting .
What to do if you get anxious

First decide whether the anxiety is something you can and want to deal with while you are experiencing it, or whether you need to discontinue contact until you have less anxiety. If the anxiety is too strong and you need to deal with it right away, work on calming your body . If you can deal with it, talk to the little one or to the protector. "OK, you're anxious, I'm here. I'm not going anywhere. If you're a protector, I hear your message. Now, are there things you can do to help that don't involve yelling at the top of your lungs? Is there something you need me to do? If not, is there anything you can do to calm down?" See also the section on anxiety in Appendix D .

If you experience the kind of anxiety that causes physical symptoms such as chest pains or fainting, thoughts of suicide, symptoms similar to psychosis or mania, severe dissociation, or an inability to sleep, or if you feel as if you might hurt someone, please seek professional help.
What to do if you dissociate or feel unreal
Open your eyes, move your body, touch something, name five things that you can see, etc. Discontinue the practice for that day.
What to do if you become grandiose
Eat some food, get some sleep, do some household chores, or do whatever else it takes to bring you back to earth. You might want to remind yourself that:
"I don't need to do anything but eat, sleep, be humble, and get feedback."
What to do if you get too analytical
If you're acting like this is some kind of technical thing that you have to get right, remind yourself of what it's really about. Put your hands on your heart and solar plexus and say,

"This isn't about doing this perfectly; it's about connecting with my subconscious mind. I want to be in relationship with my subconscious mind, not just do exercises." Then ask, "What can I do to make this more about communion and less about performance?" Then take whatever answer comes. It may be to do nothing, or to get some rest, or to do something.
What to do if you get too blissful or diffuse
Ask the bliss to become more specific. Ask it what it wants you to do.
What to do if you feel that there must be something more to know
Remind yourself not to try to pry, and to remember that the subconscious will give you the content when you have the capacity.
What to do if you daydream
Sit up, open your eyes, and ask yourself what you need to do in real life that you are fantasizing about doing.
What to do if you get stuck in spiritual bypass
Remind yourself that there's somewhere that divine love hasn't penetrated yet.
What to do if you feel that spiritual practice is not working

If you've had some genuine spiritual openings, it may be that it isn't working because your inner child is not ready to accept the love and freedom that you have glimpsed. You may feel abandoned and/or condemned by God after prayer, or hurt by the betrayal of a spiritual teacher or by religious leaders in general. It may or may not be helpful to talk to this part; but remember that you may not solve the problem by doing more spiritual practice.

It may be that you need some basic reparenting . It may be that you don't yet have any place in your life that feels meaningful enough to give you enough happiness to explore more deeply. It may be that you just need to be curious about it, even if you can't yet believe that it could be true. It may be that other people already have enough meaning and love, and that you don't need any more. It may be that you don't need any more spirituality.
What to do if you get stuck in processing

It may be that there is something real to process, but that there is also a part that keeps checking to see if it's all gone yet. You may want to find out if it's going to be helpful for you to process it again or if you are just checking. Note that in grief and in practice you may repeatedly cover the same ground without it being "checking."

If you conclude that you are checking, remind yourself that there's nothing to do with the thought but leave it alone, and go back to what you chose to be doing. You don't have to hold a family meeting every time a thought comes along; and you don't have to do any ritual to banish it before you live your life.
What to do if you feel like you're not doing anything
Remind yourself to ask the Leader what you need to do.
What to do if you do hypnosis but don't change your life
Ask yourself what you need to do to convince your inner child that you are real. Then do it.

out: Appemdix B: Neuro-Linguistic Programming (NLP)

You don't have to learn NLP to do this work. But, if you feel it would be useful to become more skilled at specific language patterns and sensory processing techniques, you may find some of the NLP information here useful. Just remember: it is a tool, and it is potentially dangerous when used to replace rather than enhance love, truth, contact, and consent. NLP is not to be used as a bag of tricks.

Neuro-Linguistic Programming is comprised of at least four layers of information. The sensory layer deals with changing sensory aspects of an experience, such as the size, distance, brightness, volume, posture, pressure, etc. The state layer is about accessing states, such as warmth, adult, courage, etc. The strategy layer is about rehearsing new, more effective strategies for responding to triggers, etc. The language layer is about learning to speak in a specific way that allows you to pace reality, open awareness, presume useful capacities, make cause-effect links, create embedded invitations, and use de-hypnotic questions to stop vague, absolute, manipulative, and grandiose language.

The Milton Model is part of the language layer. One of the problems with command language, such as "Relax now," "Stop being anxious," "Trust me," etc., is that it activates parts that don't want to comply. So, a key to Milton Model language is to speak in ways that get past the part that is engaged in skeptical arguments. While there is a subtle difference between being subtle about where you want to go and being covert about where you want to go, the Milton Model is geared toward being subtle. A good pattern for parts work is:

Start by pacing what is already true in a low-pressure way; presume small and safe capacities, and invite only one movement at a time. For example, "As you notice your body sinking into the bed, you may notice how it can feel to stop holding up the sky all by itself." Or pace reality, open awareness, validate function, presume capacity, bridge cause-effect gently, invite one small movement at a time, and always test with the body for whether this is useful.
Some specific Milton Model patterns include:

Pacing and leading : Pace by stating what is already true, then lead with an invitation to the future. "Even though you are anxious and your body is activated and this is a protector that wants to protect you, you can begin to listen to your adult self, one breath at a time." The pacing and leading pattern is a simple loop of stating the truth, then inviting a change. "It is completely true that ______________________________. It is completely true that ___________________________. And, it is also true that your adult self is here now and can begin to listen to the anxiety and the __________________________, one breath at a time."

Awareness Verbs : Verbs of awareness include notice, realize, recognize, sense, feel, wonder, imagine, picture, listen, allow, discover, remember, consider, etc. Use these verbs to open awareness without yelling at parts to pay attention. "You may notice whether you can picture it, hear it, feel it, know what to do next, or whatever."

Presuppositions : These are assumptions built into sentences. Always use them ethically to presume capacities such as choice, timing, capacity, safety, love, adult leadership, etc. "Even before you change, you can begin to become more understood."

Cause-Effect Bridges : Words such as as, while, because, when, after, before, which means, etc., connect one event to the next. Be careful not to use these in a way that is too strong. "As you breathe, your adult self can begin to hear the wounded part."

Embedded Invitations : These are invitations to small changes embedded inside of larger sentences. "As you breathe, you can let your adult self begin to listen." Or, "As you sit here in this chair, you may allow yourself to become clear about one small thing that is true." Or, "Even if the small girl doesn't trust you completely, she can begin to notice that you are still here." Don't use more than one at a time, or you'll sound like a scumbag who recently took a weekend certification.
Ethical Double Binds : There are manipulative double binds and ethical double binds. "Would you rather feel a warm glow on your body or have more space around you?"
Conversational Postulates : These are invitations framed as questions. "Is there a way for your system to let you know what to do next without having to re-show you the whole wound?"
Tag Questions : These are questions tagged onto the ends of statements, such as "isn't it," "can't it," "doesn't it," etc. Use sparingly or you will sound like a used car salesman.
